sentences.text: CORAM :
HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE E.S.INDIRESH  ORAL ORDER

In this writ petition, the petitioner is assailing the Endorsement dated 12.02.2024 produced at (Annexure-D) issued by the respondent No.2.
2. It is the case of the petitioner that, land in question is belonging to one D.V.Satish and the said land was converted for non-agricultural purpose on 02.02.1998.
It is also stated that, name of the D.V.Satish was entered as khatedar in the revenue records.

Thereafter, the petitioner has purchased the aforementioned land as per the registered Sale Deed NC: 2024:KHC:50628 dated 23.02.1998 and 'E' Khata was issued by the competent Grama Panchayat in favour of the petitioner.

It is further pleaded in the writ petition that, the respondent-National Highways Authority of India (for short,
NHAI) has initiated acquisition proceedings in respect of the subject land for the purpose of construction of Bangalore-Mysore Six Lane National Highway as per Preliminary Notification 18.09.2015 under Section 3A of National Highways Authority of India Act, 1956 (for short, the Act)
and thereafter, the Final Notification was issued under Section 3D of the Act on 12.09.2019.

entities.text: National Highways Authority of India Act, 1956
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It is the contention of the petitioner that, an extent of 23 square meters and 382 square meters belonging to the petitioner was acquired by the respondent- authorities and as such, award came to be passed on 01.10.2019, treating the subject land as agricultural land though the land in question was converted by the NC: 2024:KHC:50628 vendor of the petitioner himself for non-agricultural purpose.

The respondent No.2 has issued award notice on 30.04.2019 to an extent of 23 square meters determining the compensation as Rs.38,933/- on 02.05.2019 and again one more award notice was issued on 20.05.2020 to an extent of 382 square meters and compensation was determined at Rs.7,29,622/- and same was paid on 28.05.2020 and as such, the award notice is produced at Annexures-A and A1, respectively.

The petitioner being not satisfied with the award passed by the respondent No.2, has filed petition before the competent Arbitrator- the Deputy Commissioner,
Mandya District, seeking enhancement of the compensation and the competent authority by order dated 18.12.2021, passed award under Section 3G(5) of the Act and same is produced at Annexure-A2.

Pursuant to the award passed by the Deputy Commissioner-Arbitrator as per Annexure-A2, NC: 2024:KHC:50628 the Special Land Acquisition Officer made a correspondence with respondent No.1 and an amount of Rs.62,23,610/- was approved in respect of the 382 square Byregowda vs National Highways Authority Of India on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115204724/
2 meters of the land in Sy No.123/4 (Annexure- A3).

entities.text: Byregowda vs National Highways Authority Of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is the contention of the petitioner that, the respondents have already approved the compensation as per Annexure-A3, however, the respondents erroneously, scaled down the said amount to Rs.5,54,338/-.

It is also contended by the petitioner that, the respondents have challenged the award in Arbitration Petition No.4 of 2022,
which came to be dismissed by the Principal District and Sessions Judge, Mandya by order dated 27.11.2023.

entities.text: Principal District and Sessions Judge, Mandya
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: In the backdrop of these aspects, the petitioner has contended that the impugned Endorsement dated 12.02.2024 (Annexure- D) is liable to be quashed.
Hence this writ petition.
3. I have heard Sri. P.V. Chandrashekar, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner and Sri.

NC:
2024:KHC:50628 Prakash Angadi B.V., learned counsel appearing for the respondents.

4. Sri. P.V. Chandrashekar, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner contended the land in question was converted by the vendor of the petitioner himself and Special Land Acquisition Officer has determined the compensation as per Award dated Annexure-A3 dated 19.04.2022 and therefore, as the appeal preferred by the respondents in Arbitration Petition No.4 of 2022, which came to be dismissed by order dated 27.11.2023 and as such, the impugned Endorsement produced at Annexure-D runs contrary to the finding recorded by the learned Arbitrator in Arbitration Petition No.4 of 2022 and accordingly, sought for interference of this Court.
5.

Per contra, Sri. Prakash Angadi B.V., learned counsel appearing for the respondents sought to justify the impugned Endorsement dated 12.02.2024 NC: 2024:KHC:50628 (Annexure-D) passed by respondent No.2 and accordingly, sought for dismissal of the petition.

6. In the light of the submission made by the learned counsel appearing for the parties, it is not in dispute that the land in question was converted by the vendor of the petitioner prior to purchase of the land by the petitioner and same is reiterated in the finding recorded by the Arbitrator at Annexure-A2 to the writ petition.

It is also not in dispute that, Special Land Acquisition Officer has determined the compensation as per Annexure-A3 and same was questioned in Arbitration Petition No.4 of 2022 before the Principal District and Sessions Judge, Mandya, which came to be dismissed by order dated 27.11.2023 (Annexure-B) and same

entities.text: Principal District and Sessions Judge, Mandya
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: has reached finality.

Therefore, the impugned Endorsement dated 12.12.2024 produced at Annexure-D issued by the respondent No.2 is contrary to the finding recorded by the Trial Court at Annexure- NC: 2024:KHC:50628 B to the writ petition.
Therefore, the contention raised by the respondent-authorities, as contended at paragraph No.3 of the order at Annexure-B cannot be accepted.

However, in view of the fact that, the land in question has been converted prior to the acquisition by the vendor of petitioner, and therefore, the Endorsement dated 12.02.2024 produced at Annexure-D is hereby quashed and respondents are directed to release the balance compensation with accrued interest in favour of the petitioner at the earliest within an outer limit of three months from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
Accordingly, the writ petition is disposed of.
